☞ Purple pen time · mark and correct your answers

A skydiver reaches terminal velocity, opens her parachute, then reaches a second, lower terminal velocity. Explain the changes in the forces acting on her throughout the whole descent, and describe how her acceleration changes at each stage.

At first weight is much greater than drag, so there is a large downward resultant force and she accelerates. As speed rises, drag rises until it equals weight. The resultant force is now zero and she falls at a constant terminal velocity. Opening the parachute causes a sudden large increase in drag, which now exceeds weight, so the resultant force acts upwards and she decelerates. As she slows, drag falls again until it once more equals weight, giving a second, lower terminal velocity.
